language.script: Latin script with heavy diacritics (Chữ Quốc Ngữ) — tonal marks make it visually distinct from other Latin-script languages

terrainDescription.zh: 狹長的海岸線縱貫全國，紅河與湄公河三角洲形成廣大農業平原，內陸則有中部高原。
terrainDescription.en: A long, narrow coastline stretches the length of the country, with the Red River and Mekong deltas forming vast agricultural plains and the Central Highlands rising inland.

plate.color: white background black text (private); yellow background black text (commercial, since Aug 2020); blue background white text (government)

roadInfra.bollardStyle: No strongly distinctive standalone bollard type; red-and-white striped concrete safety barriers appear on mountain roads

utilityPole.transformerMount: Round concrete poles with small pinholes near the top and an upside-down-trapezoid pole-top shape; "holey poles" with holes limited to the lower or upper half (not full length)

historicalContext.zh: 越南語曾長期使用漢字及衍生的喃字書寫，法國殖民時期才轉為今日拉丁字母化的「國語字」，密集的聲調符號是最明顯的辨識特徵。
historicalContext.en: Vietnamese was written in Chinese characters and later a Chinese-derived script (chữ Nôm) for centuries before French colonial administrators romanized it into today's Latin-based Chữ Quốc Ngữ — the dense diacritics are the clearest visual giveaway.
